_provenance.description: Impulse SVI vs NumPyro SVI on the three continuous PPLBench models (logistic_regression, robust_regression, n_schools) under the SVI PPLBench protocol used by pplbench_configs/svi/{gp_pois_regr,scale_family_mvn}.json. New run 2026-07-13.
_provenance.config: pplbench_configs/svi/{logistic_regression,robust_regression,n_schools}.json (created 2026-07-13). Model blocks copied verbatim from pplbench_configs/standard/*.json so data matches the NUTS runs: logistic_regression n=10000 k=10 rho=3.0 seed 12345; robust_regression n=10000 k=10 seed 12345; n_schools n=10000 seed 12345. SVI harness: iterations=200 (K=200 posterior draws from fitted guide), num_warmup=0, trials=4.
_provenance.infer_args: step_size=0.01, num_steps=2000 (SVI optimization budget), num_particles=1, init_scale=0.1, guide=AutoNormal, optimizer=Adam (identical for both arms, mirroring the existing SVI configs).
_provenance.protocol: PPLBench trials-as-chains: overall n_eff = arviz.ess (min/median/max over all latent params, 4 trials as 4 chains); n_eff/s median = overall n_eff median / steady-state (trials 1..3) inference wall time; PLL = per-trial final cumulative predictive log-likelihood on the held-out test items using the K=200 guide draws. Only the guide FIT is timed (guide draws are a post-fit diagnostic), matching both harnesses.
_provenance.iterations_vs_num_steps: Top-level iterations=200 is K, the number of posterior draws taken from the fitted guide (NumPyro Predictive over the guide / Impulse svi_guide_draws). infer_args num_steps=2000 is the SVI optimization step budget. Confirmed in pplbench/ppls/{impulse,numpyro}/inference.py SVI docstrings and numpyro_harness.py / harness.jl run_svi.
_provenance.command: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' ./run_pplbench.sh --device cpu --threads 32 svi/<model>  (run without --ppls so the non-optional numpyro + impulse arms run; the optional 'Impulse (no opt)' arm was skipped by default, mirroring the existing SVI configs which mark it optional).
_provenance.env: conda probprog-bench python (numpyro/jax) for NumPyro; Julia + Reactant.jl @ d4020dba5 (frozen post-migration stack, build as of 2026-07-10) for Impulse. CPU only (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''), 32 threads.

sanity.svi/n_schools: ANOMALY (not a hard failure; run completed and produced numbers): Impulse PLL_final_mean -191634.29 vs NumPyro -6886.01, ~28x worse and out of band. Impulse final training ELBO (-7085.45) is comparable-to-slightly-better than NumPyro (-7120.22), so the guide fit converged, but to a poor local optimum: HalfCauchy scale sites collapsed (posterior-draw means sigma_state 0.118 vs NumPyro 2.898; sigma_district 0.0138 vs 2.871; sigma_type 0.309 vs 3.402) and beta_baseline is mislocated (+1.082 vs -3.243), so the held-out predictive mean is systematically off. This is a mean-field SVI inference-quality divergence between the two backends on the identical AutoNormal/Adam/num_steps setup (funnel-style collapse), not a compile/crash. n_eff/n_eff/s are unaffected (draws are internally consistent).
